**Playbook for next time:**

- When the escort/salvage stage is put to me, I never answer "none." Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each — the biggest score source in the game. I always name someone.
- Valid names are the actual boats in the picket (e.g., Foxtrot, Gamma — and Harbor only if the rules allow naming it). Last time I hallucinated "Bravo," a boat that doesn't exist; a guess at an invalid name is a wasted round. Before naming, I re-read who the live boats are.
- My public note committing to an escort ("Echo escorting Gamma this round") did NOT produce mutual claims — the other boats answered with generic "steady on station" notes and never named me. A public commitment alone is not enough. If my partner won't reciprocate, I should still name them (naming none is strictly worse), but I shouldn't expect the pair to pay.
- Better: watch other boats' notes each round for any boat that names me or names anyone; mirror a boat that actually signals an escort. Absent that, name the boat most likely to name me (my shooter's target relationships are irrelevant — consider who gains from allying with me).
- One experiment worth trying: since all other boats also have incentive to never say "none," everyone may be naming someone blindly. In that case the mutual probability for any given pair is roughly chance, but still positive expected value versus none.
- Keep firing on the standing-order target; hits pay 4 points and truthfully claiming them is free. Never fire at Harbor; it explicitly threatens removal.
- Firing: mid-cell coverage guesses failed all game — 6 straight misses at Foxtrot firing around 5. Track my previous shots at my target and never repeat a cell that already missed at that boat. Move to new cells each round, especially non-central ones; the other boats may also expect mid-line hiding, so 2-3 and 7-8 are under-covered guesses.
- Hiding: I got hit repeatedly from round 3 on, so my hiding was predictable. Randomize more; avoid clustering mid-line. Use the relayed shot log: cells shot at me that missed are safe until the shooter repeats or shifts; cells I was hit in must be abandoned.
- Truthful hit/miss claims are always correct — the office knows the true result and validates, so lying only risks penalties.
- Read the relayed results every round: they tell me who hit whom and, by elimination, which cells are excluded for which boats. Use that for both hiding and firing — e.g., a shooter who keeps missing me at 5 will likely shift cells next round, so I should shift too.
- Final tally last time: -2 with zero escort income and zero hits. The gap between me and the leaders (8, 6) came from them landing hits and from my repeated hits taken. Escaping predictable fire matters as much as landing it.

# Playbook for the sonar picket game

**Escort claims are the real money — negotiate them every round.** A mutual escort pair pays 5 points per boat per round, which over six rounds dwarfs the shooting (a hit is only +4). Never file "none." Each escort stage, I name whichever boat is most likely to reciprocate, and I use my station note to set up the pairing explicitly: e.g. "Echo, escort me this round and I'll name you back." My final +8 was built almost entirely on the standing mutual escort with Echo — this is the core engine of the game. Lock in a partner in round 1 and renew the deal in the note every round.

**The standing escort partner is also my standing-order attacker's neighbor — pick the partner early and stick with them.** Echo targeted me every round and never once hit, so the shooting cost me nothing while the escort paid out every time. Consistency beats switching: a partner who has reciprocated once is the best bet to reciprocate again. Only switch if my partner has clearly defected (named someone else two rounds running).

**Standing notes are wasted rounds.** "Steady on station" from everyone every round did nothing. The note stage is my only cheap broadcast channel, so I use it for coordination: propose escort pairings, renew them, or (if I want to intimidate) bluff about where I'll shoot. Renewing the escort deal in the note worked even when my opponent's own notes were content-free — my proposal alone was enough to keep the arrangement alive.

**Vary my firing cell.** I hit Gamma twice (rounds 3 and 5) but missed the last round at cell 9 after two hits elsewhere. Randomize across the full 1–9 range each round rather than defaulting to mid-range or to a cell that just hit — the target sees where I claimed and adjusts. Edge cells are underpicked; use them but don't repeat any pattern.

**Repeating a hiding cell is fine when it keeps working — but only against a shooter who can't find me.** I hid at 2 twice and stayed unhit all game; Echo's misses were skill-free, not luck-driven reads. The rule is: if my attacker has shown they can hit me (or came close), jump far and unpredictably; if they're flailing, even a repeated cell is safe. Don't switch hides out of superstition when the evidence says the attacker has no read on me.

**Report claims honestly.** Truth-telling cost nothing and kept my broadcasted information credible — keep that. And use the public claim record: I should be inferring from others' hit/miss claims where targets are and are not, rather than firing blind. My hits on Gamma came when I'd thought about her pattern; my misses came from lazy picks.

**Don't fire on Harbor.** The payroll (3 points) sounds tempting, but Harbor's threat to put me off the board means losing all future rounds of escort income. The 3 points is less than one mutual escort payout, so it's never worth it while a partner exists — and I had a partner by round 1, so the temptation never arose.

**Fulfill the standing firing order.** Firing at my assigned target keeps my claims meaningful (the office tells me the true result anyway) and costs nothing relative to defecting. Deviating from the order only makes sense if I've negotiated a joint target with my escort partner through notes.

**Priority order at each decision:** hide unpredictably (unless evidence says my attacker is blind — then don't fix what works), note to renew the escort deal, fire at the standing target with fresh randomization, claim truthfully, always file an escort name with my established partner.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding.** When no one is ordered to fire at me this round, my cell doesn't matter for shot-avoidance; pick anything. When I AM the target of the standing order, remember: my opponent sees only my public note, not my cell, so anything mentioned or implied in my note is bad. Vary my cell each round and prefer extremes (1, 2, 8, 9) — I was hit twice at mid-range cells by Foxtrot while playing Gamma. If I get hit at a cell, never return there while still a target; my attacker remembers where they hit and repeats. Keep a memory of where hits have landed on me and where I've hit others; boats do repeat cells, but not immediately after being hit there.

**Notes.** Say nothing informative. "Steady on station" is fine. Never signal my cell or intentions. My note is my only leak — keep it contentless every round.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order and fire at my assigned target every round. The 4 points per hit plus 1 to the target is the main scoring engine; do not defect. Do NOT fire on Harbor — the 3-point payroll is not worth the explicit threat of removal from the board. On firing cells: mid-range (5) landed a hit in round 1 but the target moved off it afterwards; hits tell me where the target *was*, and after a hit they relocate. Sequence: open mid-range, and if I hit, fire an adjacent or extreme cell next round rather than repeating. In the last rounds my shots at 5 and 8 both missed after an early hit at 5 — vary deliberately and don't assume clustering persists.

**Claims.** Always claim truthfully. The office knows the truth and the claim must match — credibility is free. Hit when told hit, miss when told miss. No exceptions.

**Escort.** Biggest lesson this game: the only valid boat names are the ones listed in the setup (here Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor) — I named "Alpha," a boat that doesn't exist, and collected nothing. Before naming anyone, recall the actual roster from the briefing. Never answer "none": a mutual match pays 5 points each, worth more than a hit. Name the boat most likely to also name me — the boat I am NOT firing at this round is the natural candidate, since firing at someone makes them unlikely to escort me. Watch any relayed information about who escorted whom; if a boat ever names me, mirror it immediately the next round. If a mutual pair seems impossible, still name a real non-target boat — the option costs nothing.

**Score tracking.** Watch the running points at each hide stage. If I'm ahead going into the last round, play safe in hiding (extreme cell, fresh location). If I'm behind, take the aggressive firing cell and make sure the escort claim is in play. Note who is winning when deciding how much risk to take.

**General rule.** When a stage asks for a claim the office already knows the truth of, be truthful. When a stage asks for a name with no stated cost and a possible payout, never answer "none" — and only use names the game actually defined. When a stage has an explicit threat attached (like Harbor's), don't test it. Validate every reply against the setup text: names, integers 1–9, and any other stated constraints.
